incident-bot: PagerDuty alert — SEV2: hosted-inference-prod latency & error spike (service=hosted-inference-prod). Escalation policy: primary -> secondary -> manager. PD incident PD-49321. Triggered 2026-05-04 22:03:12 UTC. Affected routes: /v1/chat, /v1/generate (long-context workloads). :rotating_light:

Priya (oncall): got the page, jumping in. Primary didn't ack within 2m.

Zoe (infra): metrics show tail p99 latency exploding and request timeouts from the model pool, not LB 5xxs this time — service workers hit 100% CPU and event loop stalls.

Priya (oncall): running quick check on pod status:
```
# kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-runtime
NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS
model-runtime-66d9f7c8b-6qtrv          1/1     Running   0
model-runtime-66d9f7c8b-bxj2p          0/1     Running   8
model-runtime-66d9f7c8b-g4n9m          1/1     Running   0
```
Tailing CPU profile from the hot pod showed constant busy loops in tokenizer thread.

Marcus (secondary): I was in a meeting and mobile was on DND, just saw the manager page and acked. Joining the bridge.

incident-bot: PagerDuty — manager escalation to Karen fired (no secondary ack within window). :exclamation:

Karen (manager): on the bridge. Any idea customer impact?

Priya (oncall): summarized telemetry: spike started ~22:01 UTC, peaked ~22:04, stabilized ~22:10. Approx 4-5% of requests hit >10s timeout and some returned 504 gateway timeouts. High-impact customers included AcmeCorp (prod traffic with long contexts) and several enterprise tenants. PLG users with experimental long-context prompts saw degraded responses.

Zoe (infra): I pulled the logs — a new tokenizer library (v1.9.2) was rolled to 30% of model workers in the last deploy. It introduces a pathological O(n^2) path for certain inputs (long sequences) causing CPU saturation. Autoscaler was scaling but latency was hitting timeouts before replicas got healthy.

Priya (oncall): immediate mitigation plan:
- enable degraded-mode feature-flag to serve short-context cached responses instead of full model for long requests
- rollback the tokenizer upgrade from the canary pool -> stop further rollout
- throttle requests with content-length > X and return 429 with Retry-After instead of letting them queue
- add temporary routing rule to shift 50% of traffic to the stable pool (model-runtime-stable)

Priya (oncall): running commands now:
```
# flip degraded mode
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://ops-api.internal/featureflags/degraded_long_context -d '{"state":"on"}'
# abort rollout
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/model-runtime --to-revision=42
# add traffic split
opsctl routing set-split --service hosted-inference-prod --stable 0.5 --canary 0.0
```

Marcus (secondary): after I acked I created a temp bridge and started a targeted rollback on canary nodes. I also kicked off a quick cache-warm for the degraded responses. Seeing initial p99 drop.

Zoe (infra): after flag flip and routing change p99 went from 18s -> 1.8s within 3 minutes. Error-rate falling. Customers reporting fewer failures.

Priya (oncall): marking live mitigation as in-progress -> mitigation. Customers affected: AcmeCorp, BetaRetail (subset), several orgs using long-context. No evidence of data loss.

Karen (manager): thanks. A few follow-ups immediately: 1) PD policy — Marcus missed secondary due to DND/timezone; add SMS fallback and increase PD notification volume for SEV2. 2) Rollout gating: require CPU profiling signoff for tokenizer/IO-heavy libs. 3) CS should send brief incident note to AcmeCorp/BetaRetail.

Marcus (secondary): FYI, PD sent multiple duplicate alerts — our webhook retried due to transient 504 at PD integration and produced three PD incidents for same fault. That blew up paging noise and made it harder to track single state.

incident-bot: note — duplicate alert suppression recommended. Creating follow-up ticket INF-933 to add idempotency checks and server-side dedupe within 30s windows.

Zoe (infra): infra post-action: add a preflight CPU profile check for tokenizer/library upgrades, add synthetic long-context traffic to canary tests, and raise autoscaler responsiveness threshold so replicas appear earlier under CPU spikes.

Priya (oncall): drafting timeline for postmortem. Quick timeline snippet:
- 22:01:12 UTC: CI rollout job applied tokenizer v1.9.2 to canary subset
- 22:03:12 UTC: PD-49321 fired (primary unacked, escalated to secondary and manager)
- 22:04:00 UTC: detection + degraded-mode flip started
- 22:06:30 UTC: routing split applied, canary rollback initiated
- 22:10:12 UTC: metrics show p99 returning near baseline
- 22:15:00 UTC: incident set to monitoring

Karen (manager): add these action items to incident tracker: INF-933 (PD dedupe), INF-934 (canary CPU preflight), INF-935 (PD SMS fallback), CS-210 (customer comms).

CS Ops: we'll prepare a customer-facing summary and send targeted notices to AcmeCorp and BetaRetail. Please include ETA for tokenizer fix and rollout plan.

Marcus (secondary): personal follow-up: I'll enable SMS for critical pages and update my oncall travel note. Also propose rotating secondary for overnight PST windows to avoid single-person DND blindspots.

Priya (oncall): attaching logs, kubectl dumps, and the commands executed to the incident ticket. Drafting blameless postmortem and will schedule cross-functional review (Infra, Runtime, Releases, CS).

Zoe (infra): plan to revert tokenizer to v1.9.1 across nodes and add long-context synthetic tests in CI. Also will work with releases to add perf budget checks.

incident-bot: PD-49321 set to monitoring at 2026-05-04 22:15:00 UTC. Follow-ups recorded: INF-933, INF-934, INF-935, CS-210. Closing live mitigation; moving to post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
